prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were generally too optimistic overall, but underestimated gains on several winning home wait_info tests.
Adding new screens at adoption (2 tests) or finish (2 tests) consistently hurt performance and triggered early stops.
Redesigning the adoption stage (2 wins) and choose_path stage (2 wins) proved helpful, and home wait_info updates generated four wins despite many showing no clear effect.
Finish copy changes (4 tests), finish layout changes (2 tests), sign-in hints (2 tests), and home redesigns (2 tests) consistently showed no clear effect.
Evidence remains thin for categories with only one test or conflicting non-significant results.

Changes:
0: [adoption, redesign] Carousel Friend Chooser Stage: Rebuild the pick_friend screen into a carousel stage layout for browsing available desktop companions with high-visibility preview cards. (why: Adoption step conversion is 77.7% and redesigning adoption screens produced wins in earlier experiments.)
1: [sign_in, copy] Sign-In Pet Recovery Protection Banner: Update the sign-in screen headline and hint copy to emphasize account creation prevents pet data resets upon re-login. (why: 8 support emails complained about pets missing or reset after signing in again, highlighting account safety concerns.)
2: [sign_in, reorder] Deferred Sign-In After Adoption Flow: Reorder onboarding so the sign_in step occurs after adoption_certificate instead of before pet selection. (why: Sign-in step drops 24.9% of users early; moving account setup after pet adoption increases user commitment.)
3: [choose_path, new_flow] Interactive Pre-Launch Desktop Quick Tour: Introduce an interactive choice flow on choose_path using choice cards and video previews to demonstrate desktop pet behaviors before selection. (why: Support emails highlight post-onboarding confusion around controlling and hiding pets; setting expectations early improves long-term engagement.)
4: [home, wait_info] Real-Time Render Milestone Progress Bar: Enhance the waiting screen with a real-time asset rendering progress indicator and estimated wait time display. (why: The home waiting stage has a median duration of 201s (mean 2336s); wait_info updates generated 4 wins in previous tests.)
5: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Mascot Animation Showcase: Add an active mascot animation display and playful text updates on the waiting screen while pet assets generate in the background. (why: Lessons show that adding information and visual feedback during the long home waiting phase (median 201s) reliably improves retention.)
6: [home, notification] Desktop Launch Ready Visual Badge Stream: Add a notify_when_ready badge trigger on the waiting screen that visually alerts users when desktop docking begins. (why: 3 support tickets noted pets not appearing on desktop; clear docking launch notification reduces perceived app stalls.)
7: [choose_path, hint] Companion Desktop Behavior Tip Callout: Add hint text on the choose_path screen explaining how different paths affect pet desktop docking, tray controls, and interactivity. (why: Support emails cite confusion regarding how to control or hide pets after onboarding.)

scores.note: Adoption redesigns have proven highly effective with +4.4% average lift.
Strong evidence from support emails and funnel drop; cost is minimal.
Reordering sign-in after adoption has proven success (+2.4% avg).
New flows consistently hurt conversion (-2.4% avg) and add dev effort.
Adding real-time wait information addresses long wait times effectively.
Visual feedback during home wait stage reliably improves engagement.
Notification triggers have low confidence and negative historical lift.
Inexpensive hint callout addresses specific user support issues.
